item.title: Tour: A Closer Look at "Continental Shift" — Fri Aug 14, 1:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
Join Ackland educators for a lively half-hour look at a small handful of artworks in Continental Shift: Recent Acquisitions of African Art. These engaging conversational tours offer a closer look at and new perspectives on works on view at the Museum. Free, but space is limited to 20 participants; first come, first served. This event is part of UNC–Chapel Hill’s Campus Life Experience (CLE) program. Students who attend can scan the QR code provided at the event to receive CLE credit.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: 2nd Friday ArtWalk: Extended Museum Hours — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
Join us for extended hours at the Ackland Art Museum during the Carrboro-Chapel Hill 2nd Friday ArtWalk! Each month, we stay open from 5:00 – 9:00 p.m. to give visitors more time to explore. Stroll through our galleries featuring highlights from a collection of over 21,000 works of art and sketch in the galleries using art supplies from our lobby’s art cart. Admission to the Ackland is always free; no prior registration needed. Whether you’re stopping by solo or bringing friends, come be inspired during our extended open hours!

item.title: End Negative Thinking with the Gentle Art of Self-Validation — Sun Aug 16, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group NEWS FLASH: You have needs! Ok, so maybe you already knew that. But do you know where your needs are taking you? You are predestined to live happy ever after, thriving in the paradise of a Universe that’s perfectly designed around you. OK! But how can we possibly know this? Because sequential time and separated space aren’t real; they’re constructions of the mind in learning processes. Like the quantum fields of physics, everything is forever here and now, including the highest future evolved you that’s maintaining paradise for you. Once you really know this, the journey of getting there is as happy as the destination of being there. Your only obstacle to joy is not believing in your own successful self, because what you don’t believe you can’t begin to experience. Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.

item.title: Emotional Intelligence: The Emotionally Effective Leader — Wed Aug 19, 8:30 AM — None
item.description:
For employees of Duke University and DUHS Continuing Education Credits (CEUs): 0.8
This course explores five emotional intelligence competencies: self-perception, self-expression, interpersonal, decision making, self-expression and stress management. The class encourages managers to take a mindful approach to leading people using emotional intelligence, rather than automatically relying on mental models constructed unconsciously from past experience. Managers will leave the class with tools and strategies for improving self-awareness and interpersonal relationships.
Assessment: The course will use the Emotional Intelligence Quotient® (use the EQ-i 2.0®) assessment. The instructor will send participants a link to the assessment two weeks before the start of class. All participants must complete the assessment at least one week prior to the start of the course. item.title: AI Syllabus Policies and Frameworks (In Person) — Wed Aug 19, 10:00 AM — Perkins Library
item.description:
The growing use of generative AI in producing writing, code, media, and information calls for deep discussions with students about its impact on learning. As educators, we must create sensible AI policies appropriate for our course and also engage with students in dialogue about generative AI from a place of curiosity instead of detection. You will leave this session with actionable suggestions about how to formulate AI policies and strategies to communicate meaningfully with students about AI use.

item.title: Kayak the Mayo River (2 Seats Left) — Wed Aug 19, 10:00 AM — Mayo River State Park Business 220 Access
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a kayaking trip along the river!
We will be meeting at the Mayo River 220 Business Access (Mayo River Bridge Kayak Launch 3100-3110 US-220 BUS, Stoneville, NC 27048). We will lead paddlers to the 770 Bridge Pull-out where we will be finishing so paddlers can leave their cars there, then commute everyone to Anglin Mill Access to begin. Depending on the water levels, the trip can last 4 to 5 hours. Wear clothing that you're comfortable being in water with. Dry bags, sunscreen, hats, water, snacks, and your own lifejackets if you have them are all recommended. We will have spare lifejackets just in case. Bring Bagged Lunch as we plan to stop partially through the trip to have lunch.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather or muddy waters. Message the email below to register as we have limited spaces. We will max out the event at 6 people.

item.title: Brumley Rewilding Oasis Restoration (Chapel Hill) — Fri Aug 28, 8:00 AM
item.description: TriWild is TLC’s Rewilding Program. Native species and habitats in Brumley Nature Preserve have been pushed out by invasive species like privet, multiflora rose, and autumn olive. TriWIld gives volunteers an opportunity to help TLC staff to help remove invasives, which is the first step towards the flourishing of native flora and fauna. Most of the biggest invasives have been removed (especially privet). So we have set up Rewilding Oases and filled them with native plants. Now we need to help them survive in an extended drought. Your primary tasks will be to water plants. If you have a watering can, please bring it. We will have water there, but if you have containers you can bring some water in, as well, that’d be great! Enter through the Schoolhouse of Wonder Entrance. This is a gate that is just south of Old NC 10 on New Hope Church Road. Scientists are building tools to help people and the planet deal with hotter days. Join members of UNC’s Data-Driven EnviroLab (DDL) for a fire hands-on experience around the challenge of a warmer climate!
You can meet members of DDL in the Launch Lab from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. All ages welcome. This special program is included in admission.

The Data-Driven EnviroLab is an interdisciplinary research collective at UNC-Chapel Hill that uses data and technology to address pressing environmental challenges. Led by Associate Professor Angel Hsu, DDL transforms complex datasets into actionable insights that inform policy, promote accountability, and support equitable, evidence-based solutions worldwide.

item.title: National Day of Service Clean Up Day with RiverLink and Buncombe 250 — Fri Sep 11, 10:00 AM — Karen Cragnolin Park
item.description:
Join RiverLink for a "National Day of Service" clean-up day, held in partnership with America 250 NC Buncombe County. Together, we will promote the environmental and economic vitality of the French Broad River and its watershed as a place to live, learn, work, and play.
About the Clean Up:
Karen Cragnolin Park (KCP) was purchased as a long-standing auto-crushing junkyard in 2006. For almost two decades, RiverLink invested in the property by removing concrete, healing the polluted soil, and managing invasive plants. In 2023 we connected the paved greenway path to the parks on each side and opened these five acres as a public park---one that showcases its context in nature and cultural history, tells its story of remediation, and honors RiverLink’s founder, Karen Cragnolin. Designed with flood resilience in mind, KCP performed beautifully during Hurricane Helene despite being under some 20 feet of moving water. item.title: Luminary & Freedom Stories — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — Bennett Place State Historic Site
item.description:
During this special luminary program, Bennett Place invites you to reflect on the end of the Civil War as a momentous step towards freedom for all Americans and the end of chattel slavery in the United States.
Walk among 3,310 luminaries - one for every 1,000 enslaved people in North Carolina - and reflect on experiences of enslavement and freedom. Historians dot the path and share stories of people's pathways to freedom and life after slavery & the Civil War.
---
Harriet Ann Daves recalled just how monumental Civil War surrenders were for her family: "When the surrender came my grandfather came to my mother and told her: 'Well, you are as free as I am.'"
Claiming freedom was not so straightforward for the 331,059 enslaved women, children, and men in North Carolina during the Civil War. item.description:
Do you love Haw River State Park and want to show your support of this special place?
Join neighbors, nature lovers, and community leaders for the first Friends of Haw River State Park interest meeting — an opportunity to help shape the future of one of North Carolina's most beloved State Parks. This welcoming session will introduce the vision for a Friends group dedicated to supporting Haw River State Park through volunteer stewardship, educational programming, event support, fundraising, and more. Attendees will hear from park staff about the benefits to the park and community of a strong Friends group, learn about the many ways volunteers can get involved, and participate in an open discussion about next steps.
